increment_paragraph: **UNTRACKED-BASE-NULL-JOIN-DISCHARGE** (USER DECISION 2026-11-24: "launch the null-join card"; gateway rule 83, registered by rule 74v's card; `QCore.NullJoinDischarge`; [report](../../reports/untracked-base-null-join/README.md)). `long w(const struct s *f) { const struct s *p = 0; if (f) p = f; return p->n + 1; }`, the bare `return p->n;` and `long x = p->n; return x;` were `Safe`, each under the rule-14n premise `null-deref:w:LINE:p`, while the null constant alone is `Unknown` (`unknown_alias:p`). The base obligation refused the joined binding; rule 14n's premise admitted it: `p = 0` is a known null (`Clear`), `p = f` over an unbound formal takes rule 62's custody-free arm and unbinds `p`, and `AbstractState::join`'s one-sided arm makes the result `unknown` and possibly null, exactly the premised shape. The same mechanism admitted an unguarded `if (c) p = f;`, `if (!f) p = 0; else p = f;`, a join with a member read, statements, conditions, stores, `p[0]`, `*p`, chains and copies `q = p`. The new `legacy_null_join.rs` keeps `AbstractState::null_on_path`, the names some reaching path bound definitely null since their last rebinding (union at the join with each side's definite null, removed by a rebinding, carried by a copy), and rule 14n's premise refuses them; hooks: the field, `AbstractState::join`, `transfer` around `transfer_dispatch`, `legacy_null_premise::premised`. A null-free join, a guard-narrowed non-null binding and tracked bindings decide as before, so the change only refuses more. Pinned end to end (3 registered spellings, 13 census shapes, 15 kept verdicts, 4 near misses; the change pins fail at the base) and by `joinVectors` (14 rows). Opt-in `current --monkey-linked` over Fluent Bit 046accf6 moves no status (1,171 / 2 / 3,623 / 8 on both sides, as predicted); 37 `Unknown` rows drop premises and 15 of them gain 36 refusals (more leaves than the prediction's fewer-than-10 rows). The pinned routes need inputs this host lacks and were not run. Registered: NULL-JOIN-CORRELATED-GUARD.

ledger.why: Discharged by UNTRACKED-BASE-NULL-JOIN-DISCHARGE (rule 83). Diagnosis (report §1): at the base 2a598d2af the registered spellings were `Safe` under the rule-14n premise on `p`, not by the base obligation, which refuses the possibly-null binding. `p = 0` lowers to `Clear` (target-free, known, possibly null: never premised); `p = f` over an unbound formal takes rule 62's custody-free arm and removes `p`'s binding; `AbstractState::join`'s one-sided arm (crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_transfer.rs) makes the joined binding `unknown` and possibly null, `null_premise::premised_shape`, so `legacy_null_premise::premised` read it non-null. The new crates/qcore-c-gateway/src/legacy_null_join.rs keeps the names some reaching path bound definitely null since their last rebinding, and the premise refuses them; only refuses more (`QCore.NullJoinDischarge.the_fix_only_refuses_more`), sound for any join order (`a_null_on_some_path_is_never_discharged`), exact where no path holds the null (`no_null_keeps_the_verdict`), a guard-proved non-null discharges (`a_guard_proved_non_null_is_discharged`). The three spellings and 13 census shapes are pinned `Unknown` end to end (crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/untracked_base_null_join.rs), each change pin failing at the base; formals, copies, member reads, `if (!p) return` on a formal's copy, non-null contract results and tested allocations keep `Safe`. The opt-in corpus moves no status; 15 already-`Unknown` rows gain 36 refusals. The pinned routes need inputs this host lacks and were not run.

ledger.title: A test of the name a joined binding was copied from does not narrow the joined binding
ledger.text: UNTRACKED-BASE-NULL-JOIN-DISCHARGE (rule 83) refuses rule 14n's premise for a name some reaching path bound to the null constant. In `long w(const struct s *f) { const struct s *p = 0; if (f) p = f; if (!f) return 0; return p->n + 1; }` the test of `f` proves `p` non-null at the read, but the reader does not relate `p` to `f`: the row was `Safe` (under a premise) at the base 2a598d2af and is `Unknown` (`unknown_alias:p`) at bd9aa123e, a precision loss pinned in crates/qcore-c-gateway/tests/untracked_base_null_join.rs (`near_misses_are_refused`). The dominating test of the joined binding itself (`if (p) return p->n;`, `if (!p) return 0;`) is `Unknown` on both sides because `refine_pointer_null` refuses a null test of an `unknown` binding (rule 10b). DISCHARGE: narrow a joined target-free binding on a test of the name it was copied from on every non-null path, or let a null test of a target-free `unknown` binding narrow its own binding without refusing, each with a Lean model and pins; no opt-in corpus status depends on it today (report §6).
